sourcedFrom: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) (2025)
cleanIntro: ⛔ The TR20 is Pardini's SP pistol frame built into a .22 LR rifle, and it strips the way the SP does: magazine out, one hex screw under the muzzle, barrel-and-bolt off, bolt off the barrel — and that is the whole published job. The English text on that page still says "pistol" because it was carried over from the SP book; it is the TR20's own page. Keep the muzzle DOWN for the strip and the rebuild, clean the bore by 150 shots, and keep every solvent and every drop of oil away from the adjustable trigger.

steps.title: Magazine out FIRST, then prove the chamber empty
steps.action: Drop the magazine before you touch anything else, then draw the bolt handle back and look and feel into the open chamber. Pardini prints the order plainly on the features page: the magazine comes out before the round in the chamber does, because a bolt cycled with a loaded magazine in place simply chambers the next round. The book repeats the instruction as a warning under the strip itself.
steps.caution: It is extremely important to remember to remove the magazine before attempting to dismantle the pistol.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and ‘prove’ the pistol safe.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY, printed p.7

steps.title: Muzzle DOWN for the whole job
steps.action: Turn the rifle so the muzzle points at the floor and keep it there through the strip and the rebuild. The barrel-and-bolt group comes away as one loose assembly with the recoil spring riding in it, and pointing down is what keeps those parts in order instead of on the floor. Pardini states this for both directions of the job, not only the takedown.
steps.quote: Both, dismantiling and reassembly should be carried out with the pistol pointing downwards.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY — WARNING, printed p.7

steps.title: One hex screw under the muzzle holds the top group on
steps.action: Find the hexagonal screw under the muzzle end and undo it fully — there is no lever, latch or second fastener on this takedown. Keep the screw somewhere it cannot roll away, because it is the only thing holding the barrel-and-bolt group to the action. If the group will not move in the next step, this screw is not all the way out.
steps.quote: Undo and remove the hexagonal screw under the muzzle 2.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY, printed p.7

steps.title: Barrel and bolt come off together
steps.action: Still pointing down, draw the combined barrel-and-bolt assembly off the action. It should slide away without force; if it binds, go back to the hex screw rather than levering anything. Pardini's Italian text on the same page tells you to hold the rifle in the left hand while you do it.
steps.quote: With the pistol pointing downwards carefully, pull off the combined barrel and bolt assembly.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY, printed p.7

steps.title: Bolt off the barrel unit — the book stops here
steps.action: Separate the bolt from the barrel unit. That is the end of the published strip: five numbered operations, no trigger group and no action internals. The trigger chapter that follows is about adjusting seven screws a quarter-turn at a time, not taking anything apart.
steps.quote: Separate the bolt from the barrel unit.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY, printed p.7

steps.title: Brass brush the chamber and bore by 150 shots, then patch
steps.action: Run a correctly sized brass brush through the chamber and bore, then follow with a patch. Pardini sets the interval at no later than 150 shots — tighter than its pistol books — and names lead as the thing to chase, because a leaded throat on a .22 match barrel costs accuracy before it causes a stoppage. Go by the round count, not by how dirty it looks.
steps.aside: Insure that all lead is removed to insure top accuracy and function.
steps.quote: It is recommended to do it no later than 150 shots use first a properly sized brass brush on the chamber and bore and then clean the bore with a patch.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, printed p.7

steps.title: Lubricate only where the bolt rides — never the trigger
steps.action: Put a plain lubricant with no additives on the contact points only: where the bolt runs on the barrel and on the guide pins. Nothing goes on the trigger mechanism — it is a fully adjustable unit inherited from the SP pistol, and solvent or oil in it gathers grit and moves the let-off you set.
steps.caution: Do not use solvent or oils on the trigger mechanism.
steps.quote: Lubrificate the contact points (where the bolt rides on the barrel and guide pins) with a simple lubricant with no additive.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, printed p.7

steps.title: Magazines apart every 2,000 rounds; damper rings at about 15,000
steps.action: The magazines are not a wipe-down item: Pardini calls for stripping and thoroughly cleaning them at 2,000 rounds at the latest. The thirteen damper rings are a wear part on the same page — replace them at roughly 15,000 strokes. They fade gradually, so nothing announces it; keep the count rather than waiting for the rifle to feel different.
steps.aside: It is recommended to replace the 13 damper rings after approximately 15,000 strokes.
steps.quote: At least every 2.000 rounds disassemble and thoroughly clean the magazines.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — CLEANING AND LUBRICATION, printed p.7

steps.title: Reverse order, muzzle down, and watch the recoil spring
steps.action: Rebuild in the reverse order with the muzzle still pointing down. The one thing the book singles out is the recoil spring: it must be correctly fitted before the barrel-and-bolt group goes home. A spring off its seat can still let the group sit down and the screw start, and you only find out when the rifle short-strokes.
steps.quote: Pay particular attention that the recoil spring is correctly fitted when reassembling.
steps.cite: Pardini Armi User Manual — TR20 410 - TR20 500 — APRILE 2025 (date code printed on the back cover) — DISMANTLING AND REASSEMBLY — WARNING, printed p.7

deepAbsentReason: Pardini publishes no deeper strip for the TR20. The book's dismantling section (printed p.7) is five numbered operations — magazine out, hex screw out, barrel-and-bolt off, bolt off the barrel, reassemble in reverse — and then stops. The trigger chapter that follows (printed pp.8-9) is an adjustment chapter for seven named screws, not a disassembly one, and the remaining TR20 pages cover stock adjustment knobs (p.10) and drawings (p.11). Pardini's warranty (printed p.26) states that all warranty interventions must be done at Pardini Armi or in those authorized by the company. The magazine strip at 2,000 rounds and the damper-ring change at about 15,000 strokes are the deepest work the book publishes, and they are carried in the routine list.

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & BORE
tasks: Properly sized brass brush, chamber first, then bore
⛔ All lead removed — Pardini ties it to accuracy AND function
No later than 150 shots, by the count

cleaning.name: BOLT / BARREL CONTACT POINTS
tasks: Where the bolt rides on the barrel — plain lubricant, no additives
⛔ No solvent and no oil on the trigger mechanism

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES & DAMPER RINGS
tasks: Magazines stripped and thoroughly cleaned every 2,000 rounds at the latest
13 damper rings replaced at about 15,000 strokes

reassembly: Muzzle still pointing down for the whole rebuild.
Bolt back onto the barrel unit.
Recoil spring checked correctly fitted before the group goes on — the one thing the book calls out.
Barrel-and-bolt assembly onto the action, seated without force.
Hexagonal screw under the muzzle refitted and snug.
Magazine only after the rifle is together and checked.
fncheck: Back together and empty: draw the bolt handle back and let it run forward — it should travel the full stroke without catching — then check the hex screw under the muzzle is home. Look through the bore from the breech for a patch or bristle left behind. ⛔ If the bolt feels gritty or the group will not seat, take it apart again and look at the recoil spring — do not force the screw. Anything beyond the five published operations goes to Pardini or a firm they authorise.
